findings.title: searchKey collapses null and empty-string organizationId but they yield different DB results
findings.body: `String searchKey = organizationId != null ? organizationId : "";` maps both `null` and `""` to the same cache index. In the default `getForLogin`, for `FetchMode.ORG_ONLY`/`FetchMode.ALL` the `organizationId == null` branch does NOT add an `ORGANIZATION_ID` filter (returning every org-linked login-eligible IDP), while `organizationId == ""` adds `ORGANIZATION_ID=\"\"` to the search options (returning only IDPs whose org id is the empty string, typically none). A subsequent call with `""` after a successful `null` call will return the cached set for the wrong query. Although the current callers all pass `null` or a real id, the cache key does not preserve the distinction the delegate makes.

findings.title: searchKey for REALM_ONLY uses organizationId even though the default impl ignores it
findings.body: The default `IdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin` ignores the `organizationId` parameter when `mode == REALM_ONLY` (it always sets `ORGANIZATION_ID` to `null`). Using `organizationId` as part of `searchKey` for `REALM_ONLY` causes separate cache entries (and extra DB queries) for what is logically the same result, e.g. `getForLogin(REALM_ONLY, null)` and `getForLogin(REALM_ONLY, \"org1\")` produce identical IDP sets but populate two distinct entries. The `searchKey` for `REALM_ONLY` should be a constant (e.g. the empty string) regardless of `organizationId`.

findings.title: remove() now performs an extra unconditional JPA getByAlias() on every delete
findings.body: The diff hoists `IdentityProviderModel storedIdp = idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias);` above the cache check, so the JPA delegate is hit on every `remove(...)` even when the cache is not invalid and `storedIdp` is only used later by `registerIDPLoginInvalidation`. Previously the DB lookup happened only in the `isInvalid(cacheKey)` branch. The new lookup can be guarded, or `storedIdp` can be fetched lazily before `registerIDPLoginInvalidation`, to avoid the extra DB round-trip on the common path.

findings.title: testCacheIDPForLogin registers cleanup with hard-coded alias "alias"
findings.body: Inside the create loop, `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove);` is called for every created IDP. `get("alias")` looks up an IDP with the literal alias `"alias"`, which does not exist; the method reference will be evaluated at teardown and fail. The intent is clearly `get("idp-alias-" + i)::remove`. (The same broken pattern appears in the older tests in this file but is perpetuated here.)

findings.title: testCacheIDPForLogin only asserts cache size, not the IDPs returned by getForLogin
findings.body: The test only verifies the size of the cached set of internal IDs in `IdentityProviderListQuery.getIDPs(searchKey)`. It does not consume `session.identityProviders().getForLogin(...)` and assert the alias/enabled/disabled state of the returned streams, nor does it verify that an IDP that was just removed no longer appears. A regression in the mapping from cached internal IDs to returned models (e.g. a stale entry that should have been invalidated) would go undetected.

findings.title: getForLogin does not honor organization invalidation the way getByOrganization does
findings.body: `getByOrganization` explicitly bypasses the cache when either `cacheKey` or `orgId` is invalidated (`isInvalid(cacheKey) || isInvalid(orgId)`). The new `getForLogin` only checks `isInvalid(cacheKey)`. If the organization itself is invalidated (e.g. disabled or removed) in the current session, the login cache can continue to serve its internal-id set, and the wrapper's per-IDP `isEnabled()` only filters out one IDP at a time; this can leave stale results that diverge from what `idpDelegate.getForLogin` would return.
